title: Coherent Measures of Risk
authors: Artzner, P., Delbaen, F., Eber, J.-M., & Heath, D.
verification: metadata verified (Crossref: Mathematical Finance 9(3), 203-228, 1999, four authors as cited); full text of the 22 July 1998 working-paper version read on a publicly accessible page
inspected: FULL TEXT of the 22 July 1998 working-paper version (risknet e-library, open page, no paywall involved). The published 1999 Mathematical Finance article is paywalled and was not read; the two are not assumed identical
contributes: Definition 2.4 defines coherence by four axioms the paper names translation invariance (T), subadditivity (S), positive homogeneity (PH) and monotonicity (M). Section 3.3 shows VaR satisfies T, PH and M but fails S, and states that 'the use of value at risk does not encourage and, indeed, sometimes prohibits diversification'. Remark 1 qualifies this: under joint normality the quantiles are subadditive while exceedance probabilities stay below 0.5.
relation: Needed for the engine's subadditivity guard, which tolerates rare positive diversification effects because VaR is not subadditive.
where: Section 4 (positive homogeneity, the closed-form calibration); Section 5 (the subadditivity guard)
caveats: Cited from the 1998 working-paper version; page and section references are to that version, and the citation is given as the 1999 published article because that is the version of record. Axiom PH is what licenses the closed-form sleeve scaling in Section 4; failure of S is why the engine's subadditivity guard is a tolerance rather than an assertion.
